newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit extends gains, hits 30-mth high vs Sing.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit extends gains, hits 30-mth high vs Sing.

text.p: The ringgit hit a 30-month high against the Singapore dollar on continued shift of funds from the Singapore to Malaysian currencies, dealers said.
They said international funds have been steadily moving from Singapore to Malaysia to take advantage of higher interest rates in Malaysia and potential capital gains.
The ringgit hit 1.7150/69 around 0800 GMT, the highest since September 23, 1994.
"Most of this activity is taking place offshore. There is heavily selling of Singapore dollar against the dollar," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
But gains against the U.S. dollar were restricted by the psychological barrier at 2.47.
"Dollar/ringgit hit 2.4710 twice today, but bounced back," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
He said it was possible that there would be fresh buying of the ringgit overnight in London and New York time.
In the morning, ringgit built on overnight gains on fresh demand against the Singapore dollar and a slight weakness of the dollar against other major currencies.
"The rise was mostly driven by ringgit/Sing crosses.," said the head of dealing at a European bank in Singapore.
He said 2.47 a dollar level was critical, which if broken could take ringgit to 2.46 and then 2.45 by next month.
"I don't think the market is ready for the move down yet," he said.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4726/31 a dollar. It was at 1.7170/89 per Singapore dollar against 1.7201/14 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
